clue.text: Car isn't turning left, south of local line for trains etc

indicators.note: in a down answer, being south of something means sitting below it, so the later part follows the earlier

parts.note: a local is the pub nearest your home

indicators.note: something turning is moving round, so these letters are set in a new order

parts.note: L is the standard abbreviation for line
the letters of these two words, to be rearranged
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: A complaint that a car won't turn left beneath a local railway line.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram and PORT make the lower part, which goes south of (under) PUB and L in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Buses, trams and trains are all forms of shared transport run for the general public.

clue.text: Film of soup leaves set of teeth

indicators.note: a film is a thin outer skin, so only the outside edges of the next word are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of soup
rocket is a salad leaf

explanation.surface: A skin on soup that pulls out someone's teeth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like a verb, but it is salad leaves: rocket (arugula in the US).
explanation.definitionFit: A sprocket wheel carries a ring of projecting teeth that engage a chain or film perforations.

clue.text: See 7
Perform weakly twirling round dancer in tutu, though skirts not required

indicators.note: one piece goes in the other, so it is placed inside it
the skirts of a word are its edges, so dropping them keeps only its inner letters

parts.note: tutu with its outer letters removed

indicators.note: a dancer twirling round spins about, so the word's letters are spun into a new order

parts.note: the letters of dancer, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A ballet critic notes a twirling dancer in a tutu, adding that skirts are optional.
explanation.walkthrough: The scrambled dancer sits inside UT to give U-NDERAC-T.
explanation.definitionFit: To underact is to play a role with too little force or expression, a verb matching 'perform weakly'.

clue.text: Several sporting minutes for pitcher, we hear?

indicators.note: what we hear is what is spoken, so the spelling is matched by sound only

parts.note: a pitcher is one who throws, a chucker

explanation.surface: A baseball-flavoured question about time spent by a pitcher.
explanation.walkthrough: The pitcher is not a jug but a thrower; in non-rhotic British speech 'chucker' and the polo term sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A chukka is one of the periods of play in a polo match, lasting about seven minutes.

clue.text: I don't know what my self-flagellation achieves

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a colloquial admission of being baffled
second meaning, read literally: whipping oneself results in a beating of oneself

explanation.walkthrough: The second half takes the idiom at its word: the whip does the beating, and the victim is me.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is a casual way of confessing puzzlement, equivalent to saying the question defeats the speaker.

clue.text: Tree-hugging English footballer, one great player

indicators.note: to hug is to wrap arms around, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: the England women's football team are the Lionesses
the elm is a tree
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An environmentally minded English footballer described as a great player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'English footballer' suggests a man, but England's women's team are the Lionesses; the tree goes inside one of them.
explanation.definitionFit: The Argentine forward is widely ranked among the finest footballers ever to have played.

clue.text: Intellectual leader Liz, PM with foreign money to invest: alarm about that?

indicators.note: money used to invest is put into something, so it goes inside the surname

parts.note: a bell is an alarm
Elizabeth Regina, the monarch's title

indicators.note: the alarm goes around all that came before, enclosing it

parts.note: Liz Truss, briefly British Prime Minister in 2022
the rand is South Africa's currency

explanation.surface: Alarm at Prime Minister Liz Truss putting foreign money into investments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liz, PM' reads as one person, Liz Truss, but splits in two: Liz as Queen Elizabeth, the leader, and the PM by surname. ER stands for Elizabeth Regina.
explanation.definitionFit: The twentieth-century British philosopher and logician is a standard example of an intellectual.

clue.text: Unknown quantity in series put me off, shocking then

indicators.note: something off is wrong or spoiled, so these letters are out of order
something shocking is in a dreadful state, so its letters are jumbled

parts.note: the letters as written
the letters as written

explanation.surface: Someone complains about being put off by something shocking.
explanation.definitionFit: Umpteenth means the latest of an indefinitely large number in a series, an unspecified position.

clue.text: Vehicle hit, bonnet gone?

indicators.note: a bonnet is headwear, so losing it means the word loses its head, its first letter

parts.note: to strike is to hit

explanation.surface: A vehicle struck in a crash, its bonnet torn off.
explanation.walkthrough: The bonnet looks like a car part (the hood, in the US), but here it is a hat on the word's head.
explanation.definitionFit: A trike is an informal word for a tricycle, a three-wheeled vehicle.

clue.text: Baggy trousers king examined initially, in quick inspection

indicators.note: used as a verb, to trouser is to pocket, so the word holds the next piece inside

parts.note: baggy clothes are loose
K is king in chess notation

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word before

parts.note: first letter of examined

explanation.surface: A king's baggy trousers get a once-over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trousers' looks like the noun after baggy, but it is a verb: LOOSE pockets K.
explanation.definitionFit: A look-see is an informal term for a brief glance or survey of something.

clue.text: Figure butcher's returned fisherman's device

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: ten is a number
rhyming slang: butcher's hook means look, so a butcher's is a look or peek

explanation.surface: A figure from a butcher's shop returned to a fisherman.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney rhyming slang: 'have a butcher's' means have a look. TEN+PEEK is then read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Anglers keep their caught fish alive in a long submerged mesh net, which is the device named.

clue.text: Fancy bar

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a fancy is a small iced ...
second meaning: a block, as of soap

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as wanting a drink at a smart bar; a fancy is a small decorated pastry, and a bar of soap is also a cake of soap.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a small sweet bake and a solid block, as in a cake of soap.

clue.text: A mouthful eaten by Swiss hero before a dance

indicators.note: what is eaten goes inside the eater, so the first piece sits within the second

parts.note: William Tell, legendary Swiss archer
A plus RANT, a tirade or mouthful of abuse
taken as written

explanation.surface: The Swiss hero gulps down a mouthful before going dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: A mouthful here is a verbal one: giving someone a mouthful means ranting at them.
explanation.definitionFit: The tarantella is a fast whirling folk dance from southern Italy.

clue.text: Wingers fine on the wings a day before goal netted by Liverpool, say

indicators.note: a ball netted goes into the net, so these pieces are placed inside the team name
one piece comes before the next, so they join in that order
the wings of a word are its two flanks, so only its end letters are kept

parts.note: the end letters of fine
taken as written
Liverpool FC are nicknamed the Reds
Fri is the abbreviation for Friday
an end is a goal or aim

explanation.surface: Football commentary: fine wing play, then a goal scored by Liverpool the day before.
explanation.walkthrough: The football picture hides the definition: wingers are not wide players but creatures with wings.
explanation.definitionFit: Feathered friends is a jocular phrase for birds, which are literally creatures with wings.

clue.text: Forward touching on cute header for Tottenham

parts.note: re means concerning or about
twee means sweetly or excessively cute

indicators.note: the header of a word is its top, its opening letter

parts.note: first letter of Tottenham

explanation.surface: A football report about a forward scoring a cute header for Tottenham.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forward' wants to be a footballer, but it is the verb to pass on a message.
explanation.definitionFit: To retweet is to pass on someone's post on Twitter, the social-media sense of forwarding.

clue.text: Old actress with Clouseau actor meeting poet

indicators.note: two things meeting are placed side by side, joined end to end

parts.note: Herbert Lom played Clouseau's exasperated boss in the Pink Panther films
a bard is a poet

explanation.surface: Gossip about an old film actress, a Clouseau actor and a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: The Clouseau actor is not Peter Sellers but his co-star Herbert Lom.
explanation.definitionFit: Carole Lombard was a Hollywood screen star of the 1930s, so an actress of a past era.

clue.text: Game where goal preferred?

indicators.note: letters that have erred have strayed from their proper places, so they get rearranged

parts.note: the letters up to the tail of the last word, which is set aside as the signal

explanation.surface: A question about some game in which goals are favoured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Preferred' must be split into pref + erred: the first part joins the fodder and the second is the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Leapfrog is a children's game in which players vault over each other's bent backs.

clue.text: A plot has gone awry for biblical fire walker

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: something gone awry is twisted out of place, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: a plot of garden is a bed
the letters as written

explanation.surface: A scheme has gone wrong, as befits a biblical fire walker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Has' is a link joining wordplay to the anagram's verb phrase; 'has gone awry' signals the scramble.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Book of Daniel, Abednego walked unharmed in Nebuchadnezzar's fiery furnace with Shadrach and Meshach.

clue.text: Negative response broken by a force that man possessed — when to wed?

indicators.note: something broken by an intruder is split open with that intruder in the gap

parts.note: nay is an old word for no
taken as written
the Met is London's Metropolitan Police force
he'd, short for he had

explanation.surface: A refused proposal and a possessed man, with the question of a wedding date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possessed' suggests demons, but it is simply had: that man had = he'd.
explanation.definitionFit: To name the day is the idiom for fixing the date of a wedding, answering when to marry.

clue.text: See 23
Mashed smashed — that's it!

indicators.note: something smashed is broken into pieces, so its letters are scattered and rebuilt

parts.note: the letters as written

explanation.surface: Exclamation over food that has been mashed and smashed: job done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's it!' points at the long dash printed in the middle of the clue itself.
explanation.definitionFit: An em dash is the long punctuation mark, as wide as the letter M, that appears in the clue.

clue.text: Princess married to upper-class lover

indicators.note: being married to someone joins you to them, so the pieces are set side by side

parts.note: Princess Beatrice of York, known as Bea
U is the label for upper-class usage

explanation.surface: A princess wed to an aristocratic lover.
explanation.walkthrough: BEA is Princess Beatrice, granddaughter of Elizabeth II.
explanation.definitionFit: A beau is a boyfriend or male admirer, a dated word for a lover.

clue.text: Pushy parent I'm not sure is supportive of high flier

indicators.note: in a down entry, what supports something lies beneath it, so this piece comes after

parts.note: the Tiger Moth is a classic biplane
er is a hesitant noise of uncertainty

explanation.surface: A doubtful parent wonders whether to back an ambitious child.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'high flier' seems to be a star pupil but is the de Havilland biplane; ER sits beneath it in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiger mother is a strict parent who drives her children hard to achieve, a pushy parent.

clue.text: Good plug secures the entrance of mine

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast within, so the words go inside

parts.note: pi, short for pious, means good
a plug is a promotional advertisement
taken as written

explanation.surface: A good stopper seals off the way into a mine.
explanation.walkthrough: PI and AD together form the plug that holds THE.
explanation.definitionFit: A pithead is the top of a mineshaft with its surrounding buildings, where miners go in.

clue.text: See 15 Down
A little insecure even, old legal official

indicators.note: only a small part of the following words is needed, a run of letters inside them

parts.note: letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: Someone is a little unsure about an old legal officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A reeve was a local magistrate or administrator in medieval England, such as a shire reeve (sheriff).

clue.text: Foul holes grew cleaner

indicators.note: foul play breaks the rules, so these letters are thrown out of their order

parts.note: the letters as written

explanation.surface: Grimy holes got bigger while being cleaned.
explanation.definitionFit: Shower gel is a liquid soap used for washing the body, a type of cleaning product.
